I would fix revocation and grant-management isolation before testing these patches on a daily-use phone.  I read the project docs and reviewed all five patches in ballistic-os at 82dc52d, including the surrounding Android implementation. These are source-level findings; I haven’t reproduced them on a running patched OS.  [P1] An assistant allowed to automate Settings can operate the new permission switches. The switches call the privileged setters directly, with no physical-input or authentication gate. Settings is eligible as an automation target; its SPA activity hides overlays but does not reject Computer Control input. The signature permission protects against an assistant calling Binder directly, but Settings can make that call on its behalf through injected taps.  This also lets an assistant re-enable a previously approved target: turning the target switch off does not clear the existing per-agent consent. That breaks the documented “only the owner edits” boundary. Protect these management pages from automation, or require trusted user confirmation before granting access. Target switch handler  0001-computer-control-user-allowlist-ui.patch · L239  [P1] Revoking an agent does not invalidate pending session requests. The new setter removes approval and closes sessions already in mSessions. However, validation happens before asynchronous creation and before the consent dialog. ConsentResultReceiver subsequently calls createSession(), whose preconditions do not recheck the agent allowlist.  Sequence: request a session while approved → revoke the agent while consent is pending → approve the old dialog → a session can still be created. There is also a race between initial validation and session registration. Subsequent launchApplication() checks target eligibility, not the revoked owner approval.  Revocation must invalidate pending requests and synchronize with final authorization and session registration. Simply adding an unsynchronized second check leaves a race. Revocation implementation  0002-computer-control-user-allowlist-api.patch · L258  · Session creation  ComputerControlSessionProcessor.java · L480  [P1] Uninstall cleanup misses secondary users; deleted users are not cleaned up either. The patch hooks grant removal into an existing receiver registered with mContext.registerReceiver(...). That system-user context does not subscribe to package-removal broadcasts for every user.  Consequently, uninstalling a target in a secondary user can leave its grant persisted. Reinstalling the same signed package restores the grant, contrary to the documented uninstall behavior. Signing-certificate binding does not prevent this.  Separately, the store has no user-removal hook and keys entries by reusable numeric user ID. A later user receiving that ID can inherit matching package grants. Use an all-users package monitor and explicitly purge deleted-user entries; consider user serial numbers for identity. Added uninstall hook  0001-computer-control-user-allowlist.patch · L219  · Receiver registration  ComputerControlAllowlistController.java · L208  [P2] Revoking access for one user closes another user’s sessions. Both new revocation loops match package names without matching the session’s user. Although the Binder boundary checks permission to manage the requested user, the subsequent side effect is device-wide.  Revoking package X for user A can terminate user B’s session owned by—or targeting—X. Include the session owner’s user ID in both predicates. Agent predicate  0002-computer-control-user-allowlist-api.patch · L268  · Target predicate  0002-computer-control-user-allowlist-api.patch · L297  [P2] The enabled feature still advertises version 4, with weaker session requirements. The patch intentionally leaves computer_control_support_v5 disabled. COMPUTER_CONTROL_VERSION therefore reports 4. At this version, the parameter builder skips mandatory notification parameters and the six-target limit; the server also skips the version-5 foreground-window requirement. Notification posting does nothing when parameters are absent.  This contradicts assumptions in the docs about session limits and visibility. Decide which protections are mandatory and enforce them server-side. Enabling the v5 flag alone does not prevent a caller requesting an older version. Version declaration  VirtualDeviceManager.java · L140  · Conditional requirements  ComputerControlSessionParams.java · L290  There are also two specification decisions to resolve:  Does “off” mean denied, or merely absent from the user allowlist? The latest context explicitly chooses DeviceConfig OR user approval, so the implementation follows that decision. But the Settings footer promises that off prevents all automation. A DeviceConfig-approved package can bypass that switch. The UI promise and SPEC.md’s “strip remote config” wording need reconciliation with the accepted design. Must the assistant be ordinarily installable? The README says yes, while the patches retain internal|privileged access and Settings lists only permission holders. This patch set still requires a preinstalled, permission-allowlisted assistant. AppFunctions is explicitly unfinished, so I treated its absence as planned scope rather than an implementation regression. All five patch files match the applied local source trees, and whitespace checks pass. Compilation, Android tests, and device security tests remain unverified. Existing tests cover store operations and basic Settings forwarding, but not pending-request revocation, cross-user lifecycle, automated grant changes, or version-dependent protections.
